title: Swap One Card to Even the Totals
statement:
Two players each hold a hand of point cards: alice[i] is the value of Alice's i-th card and bob[j] the value of Bob's j-th card. Their totals differ.

They will trade exactly one card each: Alice gives Bob one of her cards and receives one of his. Afterwards both hands must have the same total.

Return [x, y], where x is the value of the card Alice gives and y the value of the card Bob gives. At least one valid trade is guaranteed. If several trades work, return any of them.

examples.why: Alice ends with 3 + 4 = 7 and Bob with 2 + 5 = 7. [3, 2] works too.
Alice has 8 and Bob 12, so Bob's card must be worth exactly 2 more than Alice's: 10 each after the trade.
Alice must give her only card. She gets 6 and Bob ends with 2 + 4 = 6.

hints: Write down the totals after a trade of x for y. What must be true about y − x?
The trade moves y − x from Bob to Alice, so it must close half of the gap: y = x + (sumBob − sumAlice) / 2.
For each of Alice's cards you now know exactly which value Bob must hold. A set of Bob's values answers that in O(1).

explain.intuition:
Once the totals are known, the trade has no freedom left. Swapping x for y changes Alice's total by y − x and Bob's by x − y. For the totals to meet, that change must be exactly half of the gap: y − x = (sumBob − sumAlice) / 2.

So each card x of Alice fixes the one card value Bob would need. Put Bob's values in a set and check each x in O(1). It is the classic "two-sum" move: instead of trying all pairs, compute the partner you need and look it up.
steps: Put every value of bob into a set.
For each x in alice, if x + half is in the set, return [x, x + half].
pitfalls: Getting the sign of half wrong. If Bob has more, Alice must receive the bigger card.
Using the full gap instead of half of it. Moving d points changes the difference by 2d.
Summing a hand of large values in a 32-bit type; the totals reach about 10¹³.

solutions.title: Try every pair
solutions.idea: Check every card of Alice against every card of Bob.

solutions.title: Compute the partner, look it up
solutions.idea: Each x needs exactly y = x + (sumB − sumA) / 2. A set of Bob's values checks that in O(1).

followups: No valid trade is guaranteed. How do you detect that quickly, including when the gap is odd?
Both hands are sorted. Can two pointers replace the set?
